text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthThe What and When of Longevity DietingIt’s time to toss calorie restrictionJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CST on November 11, 2026Add Nautilus to Google“Eat less to live longer” might be a good rule of thumb, but it’s horrible  in practice. While animals living in laboratories may enjoy longer lives on calorie-restricted diets, humans living in the wild don’t enjoy starving themselves. To thread the needle, a new review published in Innovation Nutrition advances a longevity diet based on precision nutrition, with different recommendations for different ages.Powered By 1012K 00ShareNextStayCalorie restriction amounts to taking an axe to your diet, but this new approach argues for using a scalpel instead. Drawing on more than 30 longitudinal studies and meta-analyses of research on both humans and animals, the researchers sought to mimic the lifespan-boosting benefits of calorie restriction without the drawbacks. So they focused on finding the proper proportions and sources of macronutrients (protein, carbohydrates, fat, and fiber) to min-max the molecular mechanisms of our metabolisms. Read more: “Longevity Research Has a Bullshit Problem”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
